calls.reason: The forecast runs to the end of 2027. The IMF's October 2026 assessment describes resilient markets with rising AI-related risks, not a crisis that has already happened.
CNBC reported that OpenAI's 2025 revenue of $13.1B beat its $10B target and its $8B cash burn came in under the $9B target. That is a clear counterexample to the claimed 'every time' pattern.

Salesforce reports $800M in Agentforce ARR against $41.5B in revenue, which hints at a small share. But the packet has only ARR, ACV and usage figures from a few vendors, with no recognized AI revenue.
The Oracle contract mostly starts in 2027, and no missed payment is reported. OpenAI had $122B in committed funding, while FT-cited projections only suggest it may need more money before 2028.

This is an open-ended forecast with no deadline. The only counterexample offered is Midjourney's 2022 claim to be profitable, which comes before the forecast and doesn't clearly fit the billing model in question.

Even the FT-based reporting ties only one AWS incident, the December one, to Kiro. The second reported incident involved Amazon Q Developer, and Amazon says the March incidents were retail and did not involve AWS.
